race_name: Cadel Evans Great Ocean Road Ride

top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic Cadel Evans Great Ocean Road Ride's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before January.

Road-specific control matters at Cadel Evans Great Ocean Road Ride. Practice on paved coastal and hinterland roads: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 70 miles.
When someone attacks on paved coastal and hinterland roads, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
70 miles on paved coastal and hinterland roads burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
54ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At Cadel Evans Great Ocean Road Ride, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Cadel Evans Great Ocean Road Ride. Train it until it feels boring.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on paved coastal and hinterland roads can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.

Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Cadel Evans Great Ocean Road Ride. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 3,796ft of climbing on paved coastal and hinterland roads does to your power file on race day.
Varied gradients on paved coastal and hinterland roads demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.
Double-threshold training builds sustained power with less fatigue. More FTP per hour of training.

race_overlay.nutrition: Use training to rehearse an eating and drinking plan for Cadel Evans Great Ocean Road Ride's 70 miles. Start early and use products you tolerate. Use the organizer's current resupply plan for final carry decisions.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Race Simulation, Road Specific, and VO2max to prepare you for 70 miles of paved coastal and hinterland roads in Geelong, Victoria, Australia.
